# New Population Projection: How does it differ from the old one?

[Jun SAITO](https://www.jcer.or.jp/researchers/jun_saito?lang=en)
:   Senior Research Fellow

2023/05/15

#### Population projection revised after six years from the previous one

New Population Projection for Japan has been published by the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research on April 26. Previous projection was published in April 2017 and, following the five-year revision cycle, it was supposed to be revised in 2022. However, because of the COVID-19 pandemic, the publication of the New Projection had been postponed for a year.

The New Population Projections consists of a set of Basic Projections for the period 2021-2070, and a set of Long-Term Reference Projections for the period 2071-2120. Projections are provided for each of the nine sets of assumptions: combination of three assumptions for the fertility rate and three assumptions for the mortality rate. The discussion on the projection usually focuses on the projection based on the “medium level of fertility rate” combined with the “medium level of mortality rate” assumptions. The following discussion will also be made on the basis of this standard projection.

#### Aging and shrinking of the population expected for the next hundred years

As Figure 1 shows, the New Population Projection expects the total population of Japan to continue to decline in the next hundred years. Total population that saw a peak of 128.0 million persons in 2008, had fallen to 126.6 million persons in 2020 according to the Population Census of Japan for 2020. After 2020, the population is projected to fall to 87.0 million persons in 2070, and further to 49.7 million persons in 2120. The average annual rate of decline of the total population during the hundred years, 2021-2120, is 0.9 percent.

As for its composition by age groups, the population of those aged 0-14 will shrink from 15.0 million persons (11.9 percent of the total) in 2020, to 8.0 million persons (9.2 percent) in 2070, and to 4.5 million persons (8.9 percent) in 2120. Similarly, the population of those aged 15-64 will shrink from 75.1 million persons (59.5 percent) in 2020, to 45.4 million persons (52.1 percent) in 2070, and to 25.2 million persons (50.6 percent) in 2120.

In contrast, the population of those aged 65 and over will increase from 36.0 million persons (28.6 percent) in 2020, to 39.5 million persons (35.8 percent) in 2043, before shrinking to 33.7 million persons (38.7 percent) in 2070, and to 20.1 million persons (40.4 percent) in 2120. Even though the population of the aged starts to shrink after 2043, it should be noted that the share in total population of the aged will continue to rise and stay high at around 40 percent, as Figure 2 shows.

In terms of the ratio of the aged (65-) to the working age population (15-64), or the old-aged dependency ratio, it will rise to around 80 percent by the end of the projection period. Since the ratio broadly resembles the ratio of those receiving pension benefits to those paying pension contribution, it suggests that the pressure on the financing of the pension system will become more intense in the next hundred years.

#### Difference of total population between the New and Old Projections

The new Projection is compared with the old one in Figure 4. It shows that the new Projections has somewhat revised upwards the population up to 2115. It is partly due to the underestimate of the population between 2015 and 2020 by the old Projection. However, since the difference of the two Projection becomes larger towards the future, it is not only the difference in the starting point that is affecting the upward-revision.

#### Reasons for the upward revision of total population

The factors that seem to have affected the revision of total population are threefold.

#### A.Total fertility rate

First, there has been a downward-revision of the total fertility rate of the Japanese females.

The Old Projection have over-estimated the total fertility rate by 0.0862 in 2020 (projection of 1.3988 turned out to be 1.3126). Therefore, the rate for the later years have also been revised downwards accordingly, as Figure 5 shows. It reflects, as it can be imagined, the impact of COVID-19 on the marriage rate and the birth rate during the period 2020-2022. The rate is now projected to fall to 1.2853 in 2046 and remain constant thereafter (instead of 1.3973 after 2033 in the Old Projection). For the Long-Term Reference Projection, total fertility rate is assumed to be constant after 2070.

It should be noted that this downward revision of the total fertility rate of the Japanese females itself leads to downward revision of total population, not upward. The downward revision needs to be explained by other factors.

#### B.Life expectancy

Second, life expectancy has been revised upwards for both males and females in the long-term

As Figure 6 shows, the profile of the revision is different between males and females. In both cases, the projected life expectancy in early 2020s reflects the impact of COVID-19 that led to the fall in life expectancy for both genders in 2021. After that, in the case of males, it is revised upwards throughout the projection period. In contrast, in the case of females, the projection is revised downwards until 2040 and then revised upwards. As a result of the upward revision, at 2070, life expectancy at birth for males is projected to be 85.89 and for females 91.94. Life expectancy for the Long-Term Reference Projection assumes to remain constant after 2071.

Longer life expectancy is a factor that leads to the upward revision of the total population and the share of those aged 65 and over.

#### C.Number of foreigners

Third, the projected number of foreigners in Japan has been revised upwards.

Total population shown in Figure 1 includes both the population of the Japanese and of the foreigners. The breakdown of the projection of total population to that of the Japanese and the that of the foreigners is show in Figure 7

The number of Japanese is projected to fall from 123.4 million persons in 2020, to 77.6 million persons in 2070, and to 41.2 million persons in 2120. It is a decline of population by 37.1 percent in 2070, and by 66.6 percent in 2120 compared to 2020 (annual average rate of decline in the hundred years is 1.1 percent).

However, the decline in Japanese population is projected to be somewhat offset by the increase in foreigners. Population of the foreigners is projected to increase from 2.7 million in 2020, to 9.4 million persons (3.4 times the population of foreigners in 2020) in 2070, and to 8.5 million persons (3.1 times the population of foreigners in 2020) in 2120. As a result, the share of the foreigners in total population is expected to rise from 2.2 percent in 2020, to 10.8 percent in 2070, and to 17.1 percent in 2120.

Figure 8 shows that, compared to the Old Projection, the New Projection includes a downward-revision of the Japanese and an upward-revision of the foreigners, so that the decline in total population has been somewhat mitigated by the upward-revision of projection of foreigners. Reflecting the increase in foreigners in 2015-2020, the population of foreigners for 2020 turned out to be 0.6 million persons more than projected by the Old Projection. After 2021, the upward revision of foreigners increases to 5.2 million persons in 2070, and to 5.9 million persons in 2093, before falling slightly to 5.4 million persons in 2120.

Since the projection of population of the Japanese has been revised downward, the increase in life expectancy (the second factor mentioned above) apparently has not been enough to offset the impact of the decline in total fertility rate (the first factor mentioned above). It was the increase in the population of foreigners that led to the upward revision of the total population in the New Projection.

#### How will the New Projection affect the Financial Verification of the Pension System?

The purpose of the publication of population projection every five years is to provide an input to the preparation for the Financial Verification of the Pension System that takes place every five years. The Financial Verification exercise provides projections of the financial balance of the Japanese pension system, and makes suggestions on the ways to rectify the situation if an imbalance is expected to emerge in the next hundred years.

The last time the Financial Verification exercise took place was in August 2019, following the Population Projection published in April 2017. According to the standard five-year cycle, next Financial Verification should take place next year. It implies that the time available for the preparation will have to be shorter than the previous exercises. It is interesting to see how, on the basis of the New Population Projection, the new Financial Verification, will come up with projections of the financial balance of the pension system in the coming hundred years, and, if an imbalance is in sight, what kind of policies will be suggested as being effective in maintaining the sustainability of the system.

The Japan Center for Economic Research published an article by Senior Research Fellow Jun Saito (May 15, 2023) analyzing the New Population Projection for Japan (2021-2120) released by the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research, comparing it to the previous 2017 projection.

Key findings:
- Japan's total population, which peaked at 128.0 million in 2008 and fell to 126.6 million in 2020, is projected to decline to 87.0 million by 2070 and 49.7 million by 2120 (average annual decline of 0.9%).
- The aged population (65+) will reach 38.7% of total by 2070 and 40.4% by 2120; the old-age dependency ratio will rise to ~80%, intensifying pressure on the pension system.
- The New Projection shows an upward revision of total population compared to the old projection, driven by three factors:
  1. Total fertility rate was revised DOWNWARD (projected to fall to 1.2853 by 2046, down from 1.3973 in old projection), which alone would reduce population.
  2. Life expectancy was revised UPWARD (males: 85.89, females: 91.94 by 2070), increasing population.
  3. Foreign population was revised significantly UPWARD - projected to increase from 2.7 million (2.2% of total) in 2020 to 9.4 million (10.8%) in 2070 and 8.5 million (17.1%) in 2120. This increase in foreigners is the key factor offsetting the decline in Japanese population and leading to the overall upward revision of total population.
- Japanese population alone is projected to fall from 123.4 million in 2020 to 77.6 million in 2070 and 41.2 million in 2120.
- The projection will be used for the next Financial Verification of the Pension System (expected in 2024), which will assess the sustainability of pension finances over the next century.

With a projected median age of 53.5 years, Japan would have a youth dependency ratio of 17.6 and an old-age dependency ratio of 57.2 per 100 people of working age. The pyramid is constrictive: cohorts of children are smaller than those of their parents, reflecting low fertility and an ageing population.

**国立市**（くにたちし）は、[東京都](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京都 "東京都")の[多摩地域](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/多摩地域 "多摩地域")中部に位置する[市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/市 "市")。

国立町の人口が5万人を超えて、[1967年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967年 "1967年")に[市制](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/市制 "市制")が施行された[[2]](#cite_note-歴史-2)。国立町の前身である[谷保](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/谷保 "谷保")村（やぼむら）北部の森林が[大正時代](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大正時代 "大正時代")末期に[箱根土地](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/箱根土地 "箱根土地")（現在の[西武グループ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/西武グループ "西武グループ")）により住宅地として開発された。[東京市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京市 "東京市")と多摩地域を結んでいた[中央線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中央本線 "中央本線")で、東の[**国**分寺駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分寺駅 "国分寺駅")と西の[**立**川駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/立川駅 "立川駅")から1字ずつ取って、中間につくる新駅（[国立駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立駅 "国立駅")）とその周辺の地名が「国立」と名付けられた[[2]](#cite_note-歴史-2)（[後述](#市名の由来)）。

## 概要

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=1 "節を編集: 概要")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Kunitachi_stn_cherry.jpg/250px-Kunitachi_stn_cherry.jpg?utm_source=ja.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ファイル:Kunitachi_stn_cherry.jpg)

大学通りの桜並木から[国立駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立駅 "国立駅")南口を望む

 [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Kunitachi_fujimi_sta.jpg/250px-Kunitachi_fujimi_sta.jpg?utm_source=ja.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ファイル:Kunitachi_fujimi_sta.jpg)

富士見通りから望む[富士山](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/富士山 "富士山")

東京都の市域北部を[JR](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東日本旅客鉄道 "東日本旅客鉄道")[中央線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中央線快速 "中央線快速")が、中央部やや南寄りをJR[南武線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/南武線 "南武線")と[甲州街道](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/甲州街道 "甲州街道")が、南部を[国道20号](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国道20号 "国道20号") [日野バイパス](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日野バイパス "日野バイパス")がそれぞれ東西に通っている。中央線の国立駅の南側に[一橋大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/一橋大学 "一橋大学")国立キャンパスが位置し、国立駅から南武線の[谷保駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/谷保駅 "谷保駅")まで真直ぐ「**大学通り**」と呼ばれる大通り（[東京都道146号国立停車場谷保線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京都道146号国立停車場谷保線 "東京都道146号国立停車場谷保線")）が延びており、新旧の中心街を結んでいる。大学通りは[桜](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/桜 "桜")並木と[イチョウ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/イチョウ "イチョウ")並木が立ち並び、春と秋には多くの市民が訪れる。おおむね南武線に沿った[河岸段丘](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/河岸段丘 "河岸段丘")の段丘崖の上は住宅地、下は農耕地となっていたが、最近では宅地開発の進捗もあり段丘崖の下でも住宅が増えている。

かつて国立市が町制施行前の名称である谷保村だった頃、中心は[谷保](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/谷保 "谷保")であり、[武蔵野台地](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/武蔵野台地 "武蔵野台地")の崖線下の豊富な[湧水](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/湧水 "湧水")と[谷保天満宮](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/谷保天満宮 "谷保天満宮")の存在が[集落](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/集落 "集落")を形成させた。特に初期の[甲州街道](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/甲州街道 "甲州街道")は府中を出ると谷保付近で崖線を下り、多摩川を渡っていた。その後、渡河地点が上流の日野の渡しに固定されることで道筋が台地の上に移り、今日に到っている。その名残が谷保天満宮に見てとれる（現在の甲州街道からは参道を下る形で本殿に至る）。甲州街道沿いには[蔵](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/蔵 "蔵")のある農家が並んでいる。

崖線の上は大正時代までは甲州街道沿いを除き[雑木林](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/雑木林 "雑木林")だったが、[西武グループ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/西武グループ "西武グループ")創業者である[堤康次郎](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/堤康次郎 "堤康次郎")の設立した箱根土地（[コクド](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/コクド "コクド")の前身）が[中央線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中央線快速 "中央線快速")に[国立駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立駅 "国立駅")を設置し、[学園都市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/学園都市 "学園都市")構想に基づき[東京商科大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京商科大学_(旧制) "東京商科大学 (旧制)")（現・[一橋大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/一橋大学 "一橋大学")）を[東京市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京市 "東京市")[神田区](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神田区 "神田区")（現・東京都[千代田区](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/千代田区 "千代田区")）[一ツ橋](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/一ツ橋 "一ツ橋")から誘致した。国立大学町は、堤が箱根土地技師の[中島陟](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中島陟 "中島陟")とともに見た[ドイツ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ドイツ "ドイツ")の学園都市[ゲッティンゲン](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ゲッティンゲン "ゲッティンゲン")をモデルに地区開発を行ったと言われるが、堤によると、国立大学町は「最初より大学を中心として地区を定め、停車場より道路下水に至るまで理想的に都市計画を実施」したもので、「かつて外国にもその例を見ないもの」であった。[1926年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1926年 "1926年")に分譲開始。同時に箱根土地によって建設された国立駅が[鉄道省](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/鉄道省 "鉄道省")に譲渡され開業し、以降は東京[郊外](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/郊外 "郊外")の**[文教都市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文教都市 "文教都市")**として住宅地の範囲が拡大した。

[太平洋戦争](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/太平洋戦争 "太平洋戦争")後の[1950年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950年 "1950年")に[朝鮮戦争](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/朝鮮戦争 "朝鮮戦争")が勃発し、隣の[立川市](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/立川市 "立川市")に[米軍](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/在日米軍 "在日米軍")基地（[立川飛行場](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/立川飛行場 "立川飛行場")）があることから、多くの米軍兵が進駐してきたため、米兵を対象とした飲食店などが国立市でも見られるようになり、治安の悪化が懸念された。[1950年代](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950年代 "1950年代")には[文教地区](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文教地区 "文教地区")の指定を巡って街の風紀や景観を守りたい市民や学生などの賛成派と、経済発展の障害になることを危惧した反対派によって大論争が起こった。結局、町議会は文教地区指定を議決し、都に申請して[1952年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952年 "1952年")に文教地区の指定を受けた[[3]](#cite_note-3)。指定を受けた駅から半径1.3kmの地区は[風営法](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/風俗営業等の規制及び業務の適正化等に関する法律 "風俗営業等の規制及び業務の適正化等に関する法律")の対象となる飲食店やホテルなどの設置や営業に関して制限を受ける。

[2015年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015年 "2015年")[国勢調査](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国勢調査 "国勢調査")によれば、[東京都区部](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京都区部 "東京都区部")への通勤率は25.1%である。

## 地理

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=3 "節を編集: 地理")]

[多摩川左岸の沖積低地](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/多摩川低地 "多摩川低地")と、それが武蔵野台地を削った河岸段丘の段丘面及び段丘崖からなる。発達した段丘崖としては北東端に国分寺崖線、南部に立川崖線がみられる。

### 年表

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=5 "節を編集: 年表")]

* [1868年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1868年 "1868年")：[韮山県](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/韮山県 "韮山県")が設置され、上谷保村、下谷保村、青柳村、石田村が所属。まもなく石田村が[神奈川県](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神奈川県 "神奈川県")へ編入。
* [1871年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1871年 "1871年")：上谷保村、下谷保村、青柳村、が神奈川県へ編入。
* [1875年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1875年 "1875年")：上谷保村、下谷保村が合併して谷保村に。
* [1889年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1889年 "1889年")：谷保村、青柳村、石田村[飛地](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/飛地 "飛地")が合併し**谷保村**（やぼむら）が発足。
* [1893年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1893年 "1893年")：神奈川県から[東京府](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京府 "東京府")へ移管。
* [1926年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1926年 "1926年")：箱根土地（後の[コクド](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/コクド "コクド")）により、[東京商科大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京商科大学_(旧制) "東京商科大学 (旧制)")（現・[一橋大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/一橋大学 "一橋大学")）を中心に据えた学園都市構想に基づき、国立学園町地区開発。分譲開始。鉄道省[中央線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中央線快速 "中央線快速")[国分寺駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分寺駅 "国分寺駅") - [立川駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/立川駅 "立川駅")に[国立駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立駅 "国立駅")開設。
* [1927年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1927年 "1927年")：東京商科大学が東京市神田区[一ツ橋](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/一ツ橋 "一ツ橋")より移転。
* [1929年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1929年 "1929年")：[谷保駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/谷保駅 "谷保駅")（やほえき）開設。
* [1932年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932年 "1932年")：[矢川駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/矢川駅 "矢川駅")開設。
* [1943年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1943年 "1943年")：現在の国立地域（東・中・西・北）で[大字](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大字 "大字")国立が成立[[4]](#cite_note-history205-4)。
* [1951年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1951年 "1951年")：谷保村が町制施行。駅名から町名をとって**国立町**となる。
* [1952年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952年 "1952年")：東京都によって [文教地区](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文教地区 "文教地区")に指定[[5]](#cite_note-5)。
* [1967年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967年 "1967年")[1月1日](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1月1日 "1月1日")：市制施行し**国立市**となる[[6]](#cite_note-6)。
* [1991年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991年 "1991年")3月12日：[防災行政無線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/防災行政無線 "防災行政無線")運用開始。
* [1998年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998年 "1998年")：国立市都市景観形成条例制定。
* [2006年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006年 "2006年")4月3日：子供の見守り放送「[ユーモレスク](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ユーモレスク "ユーモレスク")」放送開始。
* [2008年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008年 "2008年")：JR中央線の[高架化](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/連続立体交差事業 "連続立体交差事業")に伴い、三角屋根が特徴の[旧国立駅舎](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/旧国立駅舎 "旧国立駅舎")が解体された[[7]](#cite_note-旧国立駅舎-7)。旧駅舎の部材はその後の復元に向けて保存がなされた。
* [2020年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020年 "2020年")：旧国立駅舎を解体後保管していた部材を活用して、創建当時の姿に再築された。現在は駅舎としてではなく、まち合わせ場所や展示室として活用されている[[7]](#cite_note-旧国立駅舎-7)。
* [2024年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024年 "2024年")2月2日：[脱炭素](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/脱炭素 "脱炭素")をめざす『2050年ゼロカーボンシティ宣言』の一環として、[東京ガス](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京ガス "東京ガス")と包括連携協定を締結[[8]](#cite_note-8)。

### 市名の由来

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=6 "節を編集: 市名の由来")]

* [中央線](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/中央本線 "中央本線")[**国**分寺駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分寺駅 "国分寺駅")と[**立**川駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/立川駅 "立川駅")の中間（[西国分寺駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/西国分寺駅 "西国分寺駅")は後から開設）にできる新しい[駅](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立駅 "国立駅")とこの地区に、両駅から1字ずつ取って「**国立**」と名付けたことによる。
* 「谷保」は本来は「やぼ」と読む。しかし、[南武鉄道](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/太平洋不動産 "太平洋不動産")（現：JR南武線）は谷保駅を開設した際、「やほ」とした。
* 「国立」は「こくりつ」と誤読されやすいのと、国立市立や特に[国立音楽大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立音楽大学 "国立音楽大学")のように私立民営のものを[日本](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日本 "日本")の国立施設と誤解されやすいこともあり、「くにたち」と仮名書きされることがある（例：[国立図書館](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国立図書館 "国立図書館")→くにたち図書館）。

### 昼夜間人口

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=8 "節を編集: 昼夜間人口")]

2005年に夜間人口（居住者）は72,574人である。市外からの通勤者と通学生および居住者のうちの市内に昼間残留する人口の合計である[昼間人口](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/昼間人口 "昼間人口")は71,295人で昼は夜の0.982倍の人口で、周辺の市に比べると昼夜間人口差が少ない。

通勤者・通学者で見ると市内から市外へ出る通勤者23,096人、市外から市内へ入る通勤者は15,211人と通勤者では市外へ出る通勤者のほうが多いが、学生では市内から市外に出る通学生は3,646人、市外から市内へ入る通学生は10,252人と学生では昼は市内へ流入する人数のほうが多い[[9]](#cite_note-9)。なお、国勢調査では年齢不詳のものが東京都だけで16万人おり、この項の昼夜間人口に関しては年齢不詳の人物は数字に入っていないので数字の間に若干の誤差は生じる。

## 町名

[[編集](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E5%B8%82&action=edit&section=9 "節を編集: 町名")]

国立市では、[住居表示に関する法律](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/住居表示に関する法律 "住居表示に関する法律")に基づく[住居表示](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/住居表示 "住居表示")は実施されていないが、[土地区画整理事業](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/土地区画整理事業 "土地区画整理事業")施行区域を含め、町名と地番を整理する方法（町名地番整理）により、住所整理が実施されている。住居表示実施前の町名等（町区域設定前の町名等）欄で下線がある町名はその全部、それ以外はその一部であり、その町名の末尾に数字がある場合には丁目を表す。大字は「[大字](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大字 "大字")」、字は「[小字](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/小字 "小字")」を参照。

### 独自の施策

都市景観形成条例

文教地区

市内の学園都市エリアは、[東京都文教地区建築条例](https://web.archive.org/web/20160613145103/http://www.reiki.metro.tokyo.jp/reiki_honbun/g1011298001.html)により文教地区に指定されている。

文教地区とは、[都市計画法](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/都市計画法 "都市計画法")により地方自治体が都市計画区域内に指定した[特別用途地区](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/特別用途地区 "特別用途地区")で、教育施設の周囲や通学路に、教育上好ましくないと目されるパチンコ店や風俗店、ホテルなどの業種の進出を規制する地区である。

1950年代、急激な人口の増加に加え、朝鮮戦争勃発によって隣接する立川の米軍基地が活況を呈し、性風俗産業など米兵相手のいかがわしい商売が増えたこともあり、駅周辺の環境は悪化しつつあった。街の環境を守ろうと考えた国立の市民、学生たちは、1950年12月に公布されたばかりの「東京都文教地区建築条例」に目をつけ、文教地区指定を求めて運動を始めた。

町がさびれるという反対派の声もあったが、議論の結果、1952年、国立市は東京で初めて「文教地区」の指定を受けた。

現在の、多くの学校を擁する、緑豊かで閑静な町並みは、この文教地区指定によって守られているといえる。

住民基本台帳ネットワーク 接続切断

個人情報の保護、ドメスティック・バイオレンス被害者の保護などを理由として、2002年12月26日に、[住民基本台帳ネットワークシステム](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/住民基本台帳ネットワークシステム "住民基本台帳ネットワークシステム")の接続が切断された[[11]](#cite_note-jnet_history-12)。 しかし、議会からは「住民基本台帳ネットワークシステムへの接続を求める決議の提出を求める決議」が可決される[[11]](#cite_note-jnet_history-12)[[12]](#cite_note-13)など、この切断に対する意見は分かれた。このため国立市民は、住基ネットに接続されている市区町村の住民にとって[住民票](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/住民票 "住民票")の写しが必要なくなった各種手続き（[パスポート](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/パスポート "パスポート")に関する事務など）の一部について、接続切断を理由に住民票を提出する必要があった。また、市の業務である電子証明書の発行が不可能であるため、国税のオンライン申告・申請・納税手続（[e-Tax](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-Tax "E-Tax")）ができなくなっていた。 なお、2009年2月16日に、[東京都知事](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京都知事 "東京都知事")から、住基ネットに接続するよう[地方自治法](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/地方自治法 "地方自治法")に基づく是正の要求が行われた[[13]](#cite_note-14)。

また、2009年9月29日には、国立市の住民らから、住基ネット切断により、違法な支出がなされているとして、[関口博](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/関口博 "関口博")市長に対して、約692万円の補てんと支出の差止めを求める住民監査請求が提出された[[14]](#cite_note-15)[[15]](#cite_note-16)。この住民監査請求の結果が11月27日[[16]](#cite_note-17)、請求人に通知され[[17]](#cite_note-18)、監査委員2人はともに住基ネット切断による追加的な支出を違法としながらも、支出の差止めの適否については意見が分かれたため、勧告としては出されなかった。

これを受けて、請求人は、同年12月22日に住民訴訟を提起し、約692万円の違法な公金の支出があったとして国立市に対し関口市長個人に賠償を請求することを求めている[[18]](#cite_note-19)。 2011年2月4日、東京地裁は住基ネット離脱を違法とし、一部支出の差止と支出の一部を市に返還するよう市長に命ずる判決を下した[[19]](#cite_note-20)。

その後、2011年4月の市長選挙で住基ネットへの再接続を掲げた[佐藤一夫](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/佐藤一夫_(国立市長) "佐藤一夫 (国立市長)")市長が当選[[20]](#cite_note-nikkei120201-21)。2012年2月には、約9年ぶりに住基ネットへと再接続された[[20]](#cite_note-nikkei120201-21)。

電力調達の一般競争入札

[福島第一原子力発電所事故](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/福島第一原子力発電所事故 "福島第一原子力発電所事故")をきっかけとして電力入札の検討を開始し、国立市20か所の施設を対象として電力の一般競争入札を実施した。落札事業者のエアネット（国立市発表資料での事業者名は[エネット](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/エネット "エネット")）は2011年11月より1年間の契約期間にて電力供給を行い、150万円（2.5%）の削減効果となった[[21]](#cite_note-22)[[22]](#cite_note-23)。

The webpage is a Japanese Wikipedia article about Kunitachi City (国立市, Kunitachi-shi), a city located in the central Tama region of Tokyo, Japan. 

**Key Facts:**
- **Area:** 8.15 km² (4th smallest city in Japan, after Warabi, Komae, and Muko)
- **Population:** 77,232 (estimated, July 2026), density 9,476/km²
- **Location:** Bordered by Kokubunji, Fuchu, Hino, and Tachikawa cities
- **City symbols:** Ginkgo tree, plum flower, Japanese tit bird

**History & Name Origin:**
The city's name comes from combining characters from the neighboring stations "Kokubunji" (国分寺) and "Tachikawa" (立川) — hence "Kunitachi" (国立). The area was originally Yabo Village (谷保村). In 1926, the Hakone Land Company (now Seibu Group) developed the area as a "university town" modeled after Göttingen, Germany, centered around Hitotsubashi University, which relocated there in 1927. Kunitachi gained town status in 1951 and city status on January 1, 1967.

**Cultural & Educational Character:**
Kunitachi is known as a "cultural and educational city" (文教都市). In 1952, it became the first area in Tokyo designated as a "cultural and educational district," restricting entertainment businesses like pachinko parlors and adult establishments. This was driven by citizens and students concerned about moral decay during the Korean War era due to the nearby US military base in Tachikawa.

**Key Features:**
- The "University Avenue" (大学通り) lined with cherry blossom and ginkgo trees runs from Kunitachi Station to Yabo Station
- Home to Hitotsubashi University, Tokyo Women's College of Physical Education, and several other educational institutions
- The old Kunitachi Station building (with its iconic triangular roof) was dismantled in 2008 but reconstructed in 2020 as a meeting place and exhibition space
- Landmark: Yabo Tenmangu Shrine, Kanematsu Hall at Hitotsubashi University (Registered Tangible Cultural Property)

**Government:**
Current mayor: Shinya Hamasaki (濵﨑真也), term starting December 25, 2024. The city was notable for disconnecting from the Basic Resident Registration Network (Juki Net) in 2002 over privacy concerns, but reconnected in 2012 after a court ruling.

**Notable Foods:**
Claimed as the birthplace of "Stamina Don" (sutadon) and "Abura Soba" (oil noodles). Also produces local wine, sake, spinach udon, and fair trade chocolate.

**Transportation:**
JR East: Chuo Line (Kunitachi Station), Nambu Line (Yabo Station, Yagawa Station). Central Expressway (Kunitachi-Fuchu IC). National Route 20 (Koshu Kaido/Hino Bypass).

args.summary: This is the official homepage of Kunitachi City (国立市), Tokyo, Japan, which brands itself as a 'cultural and educational city' (文教都市くにたち). The site serves as a central portal for municipal services and information for residents. Key sections include: life procedures (くらし・手続き), childcare/education (子育て・教育), health/welfare (健康・福祉), culture/sports/tourism (文化・スポーツ・観光), urban development/industry (まちづくり・産業), municipal government information (市政情報), and emergency information (もしもの時は). Notable current announcements include: temporary changes to counter reception hours (July-September, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM), the Kunitachi Station 100th anniversary commemorative site, and a notice that gift cards for price hike relief measures have been shipped to virtually all households (completed August 13, 2026). The site provides online application services, real-time counter congestion information, and a search for procedures. It also features links to various municipal facilities including libraries, community centers, the former Kunitachi Station building, FSX Arena, FSX Hall, and the Kunitachi tourism site (くにたちNAVI). The city's social media presence includes LINE, X (Twitter), YouTube, and Instagram.

This is the official website of the Japan Sport Council for the National Stadium (国立競技場) in Tokyo. The page announces that as of April 2025, the stadium's operator changed from the Japan Sport Council (JSC) to Japan National Stadium Entertainment Co., Ltd. (株式会社ジャパンナショナルスタジアム・エンターテイメント). For inquiries about stadium usage and seating after April 2025, visitors are directed to https://jns-e.com/.

The page lists recent notices, including:
- December 6, 2024: Minutes of the expert committee on National Stadium management
- December 6, 2024: Selection results for private operators for National Stadium management
- November 29, 2024: Details of the implementation contract for National Stadium management
- November 29, 2024: Setting of public facility operation rights for National Stadium management
- June 3, 2024: Selection of preferred negotiating party for National Stadium management

The site provides information about the stadium's facilities, history (dating back to the Taisho era), the new National Stadium construction project, past publications, and past event information. It also links to related sites including Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium, National Yoyogi Stadium, the Chichibunomiya Memorial Sports Museum & Library, and the High Performance Sports Center (HPSC).

# Japan's elderly population living alone to jump 47% by 2050 - research

By Reuters

April 12, 2024 4:24 PM UTC Updated April 12, 2024

REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/an-elderly-man-uses-a-mobile-phone-in-front-a-station-in-tokyo/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMTg6bmV3c21sX1JDMTE0NEZFREZFMA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

TOKYO, April 12 (Reuters) - The number of senior citizens living alone in Japan will likely jump 47% by 2050, a government-affiliated research institute said on Friday, underscoring the heavy burden the country's demographic change will exert on its social security system.

The number of single-person households is expected to reach 23.3 million in 2050, accounting for 44.3% of total households. That would be higher than 38% in 2020, the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research said.

Of those one-person households, senior citizens aged 65 or older will likely represent 46.5% in 2050, compared with 34.9% in 2020, the institute's estimates showed.

Japan, one of the world's most advanced ageing societies, has seen a constant decline in the number of marriages in recent decades as a stagnant economy hits the young generations the hardest. The COVID-19 pandemic also came in the way of people meeting their potential partners and tying the knot.

Nearly one-third of Tokyo men in their 50s have never been [married](https://www.reuters.com/world/japan/tokyo-tokyo-make-me-match-metropolis-hopes-ai-app-will-spur-marriages-2024-03-22/), while data gathered by Recruit Holdings shows 46% of men and 30% of women in their 20s in Japan have never dated.

args.summary: A Reuters article from April 12, 2024, reports that the number of senior citizens living alone in Japan will likely jump 47% by 2050, according to Japan's National Institute of Population and Social Security Research. Single-person households are expected to reach 23.3 million in 2050, accounting for 44.3% of total households (up from 38% in 2020). Senior citizens aged 65 or older will represent 46.5% of one-person households in 2050, compared to 34.9% in 2020. The article notes that Japan is one of the world's most advanced aging societies, with a constant decline in marriages due to a stagnant economy hitting young generations hardest. Nearly one-third of Tokyo men in their 50s have never been married, and data shows 46% of men and 30% of women in their 20s in Japan have never dated.

# Japan’s Population Will Rapidly Age and Shrink by 20 Percent by 2050

 October 18, 2019

By: [East Asia Forum](https://nationalinterest.org/profile/east-asia-forum)

### Share

*   [Share this link on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnationalinterest.org%2Fblog%2Fbuzz%2Fjapans-population-will-rapidly-age-and-shrink-20-percent-2050-89551%3Futm_source%3Dfacebook)
*   [Share this page on X (Twitter)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnationalinterest.org%2Fblog%2Fbuzz%2Fjapans-population-will-rapidly-age-and-shrink-20-percent-2050-89551%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_campaign%3Dweb-share)
*   [Share this link on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnationalinterest.org%2Fblog%2Fbuzz%2Fjapans-population-will-rapidly-age-and-shrink-20-percent-2050-89551%3Futm_source%3Dlinkedin%26utm_campaign%3Dweb-share)
*   [Share this page on Reddit](https://reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnationalinterest.org%2Fblog%2Fbuzz%2Fjapans-population-will-rapidly-age-and-shrink-20-percent-2050-89551%3Futm_source%3Dreddit%26utm_campaign%3Dweb-share&title=Japan%27s+Population+Will+Rapidly+Age+and+Shrink+by+20+Percent+by+2050)
*   [Email a link to this page](mailto:?body=https%3A%2F%2Fnationalinterest.org%2Fblog%2Fbuzz%2Fjapans-population-will-rapidly-age-and-shrink-20-percent-2050-89551%3Futm_source%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3Dweb-share&subject=Japan%27s+Population+Will+Rapidly+Age+and+Shrink+by+20+Percent+by+2050)

Population projections from the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs confirm that Japan will remain the world’s most aged country for at least the next few decades.[The 2019 Revision of World Population Prospects](https://population.un.org/wpp/), released in June 2019, predicts the proportion of people aged 65 years and older in Japan will increase from the current level of 28 per cent to 38 per cent by 2050.

During this period, Japan’s population will shrink by nearly 20 per cent. These demographic trends set the fundamental context for challenges and changes to Japanese society in the coming decades.

Japan’s population has been getting older over the past 100 years, but this process accelerated at the turn of the century when the large cohort of post-war baby boomers, born in the late 1940s to early 1950s, began joining the elderly population. Between 2000–10, the country’s population aged 65 and over increased by an unprecedented 7 million. This population is likely to increase by another 7 million by 2020.

According to the government’s official[population projections](http://www.ipss.go.jp/pp-zenkoku/e/zenkoku_e2017/pp_zenkoku2017e.asp)conducted by the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research (IPSS), the elderly population will continue to grow — though at a slower pace — until it peaks at around 2040, when the second baby-boomer generation (the children of the post-war baby boomers) passes the age of 65. At this time, a much smaller younger population will face the task of supporting this large number of elderly Japanese.

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

The conventional indicator of an aging population — the proportion of people aged 65 and over — may lead to its extent and impacts in Japan being underestimated.[IPSS projections](http://www.ipss.go.jp/pp-zenkoku/e/zenkoku_e2017/pp_zenkoku2017e.asp)suggest that the country’s population aged 75 and over will increase by 20 per cent from 2020 to 2040, while the increase will be limited to around 8 per cent for those aged 65 and over. The most significant growth is projected for the ‘oldest old population’: 65 per cent for those aged 85 and over, and more than 250 per cent for those aged 100 and over.

The ‘aging of the elderly population’ has serious implications for the public systems of medical and long-term care, pensions and social protection for older people. Much attention is being paid to the provision of care services, and in this regard knowing where older people live is fundamental to ensuring appropriate public policy and community responses.[IPSS projections](http://www.ipss.go.jp/pp-shicyoson/e/shicyoson18/t-page.asp)expect the most significant growth in Japan’s elderly population to occur in metropolitan regions, where there are currently relatively large working-age populations.

In some prefectures in non-metropolitan regions, on the other hand, the size of the elderly population has already peaked and started to decline. In these areas, the proportion of the elderly in the local population continues to increase because the younger component is shrinking at an even faster pace.

These regional variations in demographic prospects are due to heterogeneity in the population structure, rather than trends in vital components of population change such as mortality and fertility. Despite efforts by local governments to recover the fertility rate and reverse population flows to large cities, the rural population profile has become ‘too old’ to restructure in the short term. The aging population problem has reached the stage where the skewed age distribution causes negative natural increases (numbers of deaths exceeding numbers of births).

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

Aging and depopulation in these rural and non-metropolitan regions result in diminishing pools of potential young migrants to major metropolitan regions, particularly the Tokyo metropolitan region. Tokyo has the lowest fertility level in the country and its current population growth is sustained by population inflows.[IPSS projections](http://www.ipss.go.jp/pp-shicyoson/e/shicyoson18/t-page.asp)expect Tokyo to maintain its population growth until around 2030, before it becomes the last prefecture to enter population decline.

At the national level, Japan’s depopulation is moderated by the growing number of foreign residents, who presently account for just over 2 per cent of the country’s total population. As Japan’s natural population decline escalates, expectations have been rising for demographic and labour-market contributions to be made by[international migrants](https://www.eastasiaforum.org/2018/11/15/genuine-immigration-still-alien-to-japan/). In the face of acute labour shortages, the amended Immigration Act came into effect in April 2019 to introduce new visa categories for qualified[foreign workers](https://www.eastasiaforum.org/2019/06/19/japan-opens-its-doors-to-foreign-labour/)in 14 industrial sectors, including nursing care, agriculture, construction and manufacturing.

The new visa categories are probably the most significant change in Japan’s immigration policy since the 1990 amendment that removed restrictions on entry and residence for foreign-born people of Japanese descent to facilitate economically-motivated migration from South America. It is hoped that the 2019 amendment will increase the pool of nursing and care workers, presumably from Southeast Asian countries.

It is still too early to assess the impact of the 2019 amendment to the Immigration Act. From a demographic perspective, it is important to keep in mind that the ‘targeted sending countries’ will face labour shortages themselves, particularly of care workers, in the not-so-distant future.

According to the latest UN population projections, many[Southeast Asian countries will undergo population aging](https://www.eastasiaforum.org/2019/03/17/burden-sharing-a-remedy-for-falling-birth-rates-in-east-asia/)at an even faster pace than Japan due to drastic declines in fertility. What is expected from the global front-runner in aging are lessons and solutions from its evolving experience in building and maintaining public systems for an aging society.

_Masataka Nakagawa is Senior Researcher at the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research (IPSS), Tokyo._

args.key_excerpts: The 2019 Revision of World Population Prospects predicts the proportion of people aged 65 years and older in Japan will increase from the current level of 28 per cent to 38 per cent by 2050; During this period, Japan's population will shrink by nearly 20 per cent; The most significant growth is projected for the 'oldest old population': 65 per cent for those aged 85 and over, and more than 250 per cent for those aged 100 and over; Tokyo has the lowest fertility level in the country and its current population growth is sustained by population inflows; What is expected from the global front-runner in aging are lessons and solutions from its evolving experience in building and maintaining public systems for an aging society.
args.summary: This article from The National Interest (originally published on East Asia Forum, October 2019) reports on Japan's severe demographic crisis. According to UN population projections, Japan will remain the world's most aged country for decades. The proportion of people aged 65+ will rise from 28% to 38% by 2050, while the total population will shrink by nearly 20%. The post-war baby boomer cohort accelerated this aging trend after 2000. The "oldest old" population is growing fastest: those 85+ will increase by 65%, and those 100+ by over 250% by 2040. Regional disparities exist, with metropolitan areas seeing growth in elderly populations while non-metropolitan regions have already peaked and are declining. Tokyo's population growth is sustained by inflows but is expected to decline after 2030. Foreign residents (currently just over 2% of the population) are moderating depopulation. The 2019 amendment to the Immigration Act introduced new visa categories for foreign workers in 14 sectors, including nursing care. However, Southeast Asian countries—the likely source of workers—will face their own aging challenges soon. The author, Masataka Nakagawa, is a Senior Researcher at Japan's National Institute of Population and Social Security Research (IPSS).
